runs.title: Alex Karp: what did he actually say?
runs.prompt: Palantir CEO Alex Karp is in the news for reportedly saying that only two kinds of people will succeed in the AI era. runs.answer:
Palantir CEO Alex Karp said: "There are basically two ways to know you have a future… One, you have some vocational training. Or two, you're neurodivergent." He added that AI-era success favors people who are "more of an artist, look at things from a different direction, be able to build something unique," and (per Livemint) that "neurodivergent" is "broadly defined."

Context: it came from a March 2026 interview on TBPN, the live tech talk show hosted by John Coogan and Jordi Hays (full episode: "FULL INTERVIEW: Alex Karp on AI, Job Loss, and the Future of Work"; clip at youtube.com/watch?v=Kz52OYklzvw). Fortune's write-up says he "said on TBPN in March." The Livemint article was published 26 March 2026.

runs.answer: Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is not a new standalone game — "Dark Arisen" is a paid expansion/DLC for Dragon's Dogma 2, and the name also refers to the bundle/edition that packages the base game plus that expansion (plus the Explorer's Camping Kit and a Custom Sounds pack). It releases the night of Thursday Oct 8, 2026, 5:00 PM PDT / Friday Oct 9, 2026 (1:00 AM BST; worldwide date Oct 9, 2026) on PS5, Windows/PC (Steam), Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. Pricing (US): the Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen bundle is $49.99; the standalone Dark Arisen Expansion add-on is $29.99; the base Dragon's Dogma 2 is $39.99; the two extra items are $2.99 each. The expansion adds a new snowy northern region, Norgan ("Forsaken Dominion"), with the character Eir and the "Fallen Dragon," plus "Lost Rites," 12 new dungeon challenges in the main area. It's marked PS5 Pro Enhanced and optimized for Xbox Series X|S.

runs.title: Best readable source for Yorkshire tiger incident
runs.prompt: The Yorkshire Wildlife Park tiger incident of 10 October 2026 is being covered by many UK outlets, several of which block automated readers or paywall. Compare these four candidate sources and recommend the best one for a reader who wants the key facts (what happened, official statements, whether the park is closed) without hitting a paywall or registration wall: theguardian.com, yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk, metro.co.uk, and independent.co.uk. Visit each candidate's story and report which ones you could actually read.
runs.answer: Three of the four were readable with no paywall or registration wall; only the Yorkshire Evening Post was blocked (HTTP 403, Cloudflare-style "Just a moment..." bot challenge). The Guardian, Metro and The Independent all loaded in full — each reporting the key facts: a man climbed into the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Sat 10 Oct, was attacked and pronounced dead at the scene; South Yorkshire Police said the tiger was uninjured and there was no wider public risk; and the park was evacuated and closed for the weekend. Best pick for a reader who just wants the key facts cleanly: theguardian.com — a single concise article carrying the police statement, the park's statement and the closure, with no paywall and no interstitials. Metro (also fully readable) is a good alternative with a bit more colour, and The Independent works too but is a live blog with membership/donation prompts.

runs.title: Pick the best Singapore GP times source
runs.prompt: Formula 1's Singapore Grand Prix weekend (10-12 October 2026) has had schedule changes because of rain, and fans want the revised session times in UK time. Compare these four candidate sites and pick the clearest, most reliable one for finding the revised sprint, qualifying, and race times: formula1.com, grandprixpal.com, scuderiafans.com, and sportsbrackets.net. Visit each candidate's Singapore GP page and note which ones loaded and which blocked you.
runs.answer: Pick formula1.com: it loaded instantly, is the official source, lists every session with a "My Time / Track Time" toggle (UK viewers see BST), and its own news confirms the rain-hit Singapore Sprint — with grandprixpal.com the clear runner-up since it also loaded and offers an explicit "London (GMT/BST)" timezone selector. The other two failed or disappointed: scuderiafans.com returned an HTTP 403 Cloudflare "Just a moment..." bot wall (blocked), and sportsbrackets.net returned 200 but buried the actual article under a giant US-sports menu so the schedule body never appeared (and its times are US-oriented). UK (BST, UTC+1) times for the sprint weekend — note the dates are Fri 9–Sun 11 Oct 2026, not 10–12 — are: FP1 Fri 09:30–10:30, Sprint Qualifying Fri 13:30–14:14, Sprint Sat 10:00–11:00, Qualifying Sat 14:30–15:30, Grand Prix Sun 13:00 BST (grandprixpal lists qualifying 30 min earlier, 14:00). One caveat: I found no page explicitly documenting a rain-driven schedule revision; the schedules shown are the standard sprint timetable, and the sprint race itself was the rain-affected session.
